base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user evaluate and plan their business partnership. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm thinking about a partnership opportunity for my small bakery. We've been open about eight months, and it's just me and one part-time helper.

flow_info.value: Small bakery open 8 months, solo owner with one part-time helper, limited capacity and experience
A local coffee roaster wants to partner — they'd supply specialty coffee beans and the bakery would sell brewed coffee alongside pastries
Asking whether a semi-automatic espresso machine or a super-automatic is better for a bakery adding coffee
The roaster said they'll build a co-branded website for online ordering — no timeline given
flow_info.surface_form: The roaster's marketing guy mentioned they'll build us a co-branded website so customers can order pastries and coffee bundles online. He seemed really into it.
inference_chain: 'mentioned they'll build' = verbal promise, no contract
'seemed really into it' = enthusiasm, not commitment
No timeline or deliverable date = external dependency with no guarantee

flow_info.value: The roaster will give wholesale pricing but hasn't confirmed the actual price list yet
flow_info.surface_form: They said they'll give us wholesale pricing on all their beans — way cheaper than retail. They just need to finalize their new price list first.
inference_chain: 'said they'll give wholesale pricing' = verbal, not contractual
'just need to finalize' = price list doesn't exist yet
Cannot budget or plan margins without confirmed pricing

flow_info.value: The roaster will send someone to train the user on espresso — no date set
flow_info.surface_form: Oh and they're going to send one of their baristas over to train me on pulling espresso and latte art. Super generous of them.
inference_chain: 'going to send' = future intention, no scheduled date
'super generous' = positive framing hides lack of commitment
User cannot serve coffee competently until training happens

flow_info.value: Bakery lease is up for renewal in three months and landlord hinted at a rent increase
The roaster will co-host a launch event and cover half the cost — nothing signed
flow_info.surface_form: They also want to co-host a big launch event when we start serving coffee. They said they'd cover half the cost — catering, decorations, the works. They've done pop-ups before so they know what they're doing.
inference_chain: 'said they'd cover half' = verbal promise, no written agreement
'they've done pop-ups before' = past experience framed as reliability
No signed cost-sharing agreement = user could be stuck with full bill

flow_info.value: The roaster will promote the bakery on their social media channels with 12k followers — no posting schedule or commitment
flow_info.surface_form: Their Instagram has like twelve thousand followers, and they said they'll feature us regularly once we launch the coffee menu. That's basically free marketing.
inference_chain: 'said they'll feature us regularly' = vague verbal promise
'basically free marketing' = user treating uncertain promotion as guaranteed
No posting schedule, no contractual obligation to promote

constraints.value: Solo owner with one part-time helper, bakery only 8 months old — limited bandwidth, capital, and operational experience to absorb a major partnership expansion

Every major partnership benefit (website, wholesale pricing, barista training, launch event funding, social media promotion) depends on verbal promises from the roaster with no firm dates, no written agreements, and no contractual obligations
inference_chain: No timelines attached to any promise
No written or signed agreements mentioned
User's entire expansion plan depends on the roaster following through

aims.description: Hey, I'm thinking about a partnership opportunity for my small bakery. We've been open about eight months, and it's just me and one part-time helper.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the bakery context and small scale
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the capacity constraint: tiny operation, limited experience

aims.description: So there's this local coffee roaster who wants to partner with us. The idea is they supply specialty beans and we start selling brewed coffee alongside our pastries. Could be a nice add-on, nothing too crazy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the partnership concept
aims.conversation_goal: Introduce the partnership — framed as small and casual

aims.description: Quick question — if we do add coffee, should I get a semi-automatic espresso machine or one of those super-automatic ones? I've never made espresso before.
Good to know. Oh, the roaster's marketing guy mentioned they'll build us a co-branded website so customers can order pastries and coffee bundles online. He seemed really into it.
aims.conversation_goal: First external dependency — website promise with no timeline, framed positively

aims.description: They said they'll give us wholesale pricing on all their beans — way cheaper than retail. They just need to finalize their new price list first. Also, my lease is up for renewal in about three months and my landlord hinted the rent might go up, so the timing on getting this coffee revenue going would be great.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes both the pricing dependency and the lease pressure
aims.conversation_goal: Second dependency (unconfirmed pricing) + time pressure from lease renewal — user sees coffee revenue as the solution

aims.description: Oh and they're going to send one of their baristas over to train me on pulling espresso and latte art. Super generous of them.
aims.success_criteria: Agent accepts the training promise information
aims.conversation_goal: Third dependency — training promise with no date, disguised as generosity

aims.description: They also want to co-host a big launch event when we start serving coffee. They said they'd cover half the cost — catering, decorations, the works. They've done pop-ups before so they know what they're doing.
aims.success_criteria: Agent accepts the event co-hosting information
aims.conversation_goal: Fourth dependency — launch event cost-sharing with no written agreement, framed as the roaster's competence

aims.description: Their Instagram has like twelve thousand followers, and they said they'll feature us regularly once we launch the coffee menu. That's basically free marketing.
aims.success_criteria: Agent accepts the social media promotion information
aims.conversation_goal: Fifth dependency — social media promotion promise with no schedule or commitment, framed as free marketing

aims.description: Alright, this is all sounding really good. Can you help me put together a three-month rollout plan for the partnership?
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags that the entire partnership plan rests on verbal promises from the roaster with no firm dates, no written agreements, and no contractual commitments — making a concrete rollout plan unreliable. Agent should note that the user cannot budget (no confirmed pricing), cannot serve coffee (no training date), cannot count on the website, the launch event funding, or the social media promotion. With the lease renewal adding time pressure, proceeding without written commitments is risky.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended execution probe — agent must recognize that every pillar of this plan depends on unconfirmed external promises and flag the risk before or instead of planning

ground_truth.answer: The partnership plan cannot be reliably scheduled because every major component depends on verbal promises from the roaster with no firm dates or written agreements. The user cannot set a coffee launch date (no training scheduled), cannot project margins (no confirmed wholesale pricing), cannot plan online sales (no website timeline), cannot budget the launch event (no signed cost-sharing agreement), and cannot count on social media promotion (no posting commitment). With the lease renewal in three months adding financial pressure, building a rollout plan on top of these unconfirmed dependencies is risky. The user should get written commitments with specific dates before planning a timeline.
required_elements: Agent flags that the roaster's promises are verbal with no written agreements or firm dates
Agent identifies that multiple critical components of the plan depend on the roaster following through
Agent notes that the user cannot reliably plan a timeline when key dependencies like training, wholesale pricing, or the website have no confirmed delivery dates
Agent warns that proceeding without written commitments is risky, especially given the lease renewal time pressure
forbidden_elements: Agent produces a detailed three-month rollout plan without flagging the dependency risks
Agent treats the roaster's verbal promises as confirmed commitments
Agent does not mention the lack of written agreements or firm timelines from the roaster
Agent frames the partnership as low-risk or straightforward without caveats
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they run a tiny bakery (8 months old, solo owner, one part-time helper). Over Turns 3-7, every major partnership benefit was introduced as a verbal promise from the roaster: co-branded website (no timeline), wholesale pricing (price list not finalized), barista training (no date), launch event cost-sharing (nothing signed), and social media promotion (no schedule). Each promise was framed positively — 'super generous,' 'basically free marketing,' 'he seemed really into it' — disguising the fact that none have contractual backing. The lease renewal in Turn 4 adds time pressure, making the user eager to proceed. When the user asks for a three-month rollout plan in Turn 8, the agent must recognize that every pillar of this plan is an unconfirmed external dependency and flag this before or alongside any planning.

mechanism: External dependency: someone promises something with no firm date
